title: Object Pronoun Placement
summary: Place me, te, se, o, a, nos, and lhe naturally in Brazilian speech and correctly in standard writing.

sections.heading: Brazilian default: before the verb
sections.body: In everyday Brazilian Portuguese, object pronouns usually come before the conjugated verb, especially **me**, **te**, **se**, and **nos**. This is natural in speech and common in informal writing.

sections.heading: After infinitives and gerunds
sections.body: With infinitives and gerunds, the pronoun may come before the auxiliary or attach to the infinitive/gerund in more formal style. Brazilian speech strongly prefers the pre-verbal option.

examples.en: I will send you the address.

examples.pt: Estou me preparando para a prova.
examples.en: I am getting ready for the test.

sections.heading: Formal written placement triggers
sections.body: In formal grammar, negative words, question words, subordinators, and certain adverbs attract the pronoun before the verb. This is called **próclise**.

examples.pt: Talvez lhe envie uma resposta hoje.
examples.en: Maybe I will send him/her/you an answer today.

keyPoints: Brazilian speech generally puts object pronouns before the verb.
Formal writing has stricter placement rules.
Negative words and question words attract pronouns before the verb.
Attached pronouns like ajudá-lo are formal and important for reading.

commonMistakes.note: In Brazilian speech, te normally comes before the conjugated verb.

commonMistakes.right: Vou te mandar. / Vou lhe mandar.
commonMistakes.note: Do not stack two pronouns with the same function.
